To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
We provide a unified analysis of generalization bounds of robust optimization, which is applicable to both stochastic and adversarially robust optimization.

(i) we provide a general framework for generalization analysis of robust optimization and Wasserstien robust optimization, (ii) the framework can be used to derive generalization bounds under stochastic and adversarial settings, (iii) we show that robustness can be achieved by adding variation regularization, and the regularization strength is related to the robustness level, and (iv) we provide generalization bounds for Wasserstien robustness under the transportation information inequality assumption

we derive generalization guarantees for distributionally robust optimization and Wassersten robust optimization for Lipschtz and piecewise Höler smooth loss functions under stochastic and adversarial settings, assuming that the data distribution satisfies transportation information inequalities.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following questions: What is the generalization bound for (Wasserstain) robust optimization? How does robustness connect to generalization bounds for (Wassersteins) robust optimization? What is the generalizaiton bound for (Wassersstein) robust optimization with Lipschitz or Hölder smooth loss function? What is the relationship between robustness and variation regularization?
the following two aspects: (1) generalization bounds for (Wasserstain) robust optimization; (2) generalization bounds of variation regularization and their connection with robust optimization.

the following questions: (i) What is the generalization error of robust optimization under transportation-information inequalities? (ii) How does the generalization error depend on the regularization strength of Lipschitz and gradient regularizations, and the Wasserstein distance between the empirical distribution and the underlying data distribution?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

(1) robust optimization and Wasserstien robust optimization are generalization enhancing; (2) robust optimization is more generalizable than Wasserstein robust optimization; and (3) robust optimization can be more robust than Wasserstein robustness.

, under transportation-information inequalities, we can obtain a generalization bound with the same order of magnitude as in the non-robust setting, and it does not depend on the number of training samples or the robustness level.
, under the same assumption, the generalization bound of robust optimization is no worse than that of non-robust optimization.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we establish the connection between robustness and variation regularization.
we show that the robust optimization is equivalent to the variation regularization and the Wasserstein robust optimization is equivalent with the variation regularization under a Wasserstein metric.

the robustness of a learning algorithm can be characterized by the variation regularizer and the robustness of the algorithm can be characterized in terms of the transportation-information inequalities.
The main takeaway from our work is that
robust optimization and Wasserstien robust optimization can be viewed as generalization of variation regularization.
the Wasserstein robust optimization can be viewed as a generalization of Lipschitz regularized empirical risk minimization, which provides a theoretical explanation to its empirical success.
robustness can be understood as a special case of variation regularization.
